text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Gallic warmth greets Jean Chretien: Doors open for once-snubbed PM as France, Canada find reasons to get along.
- Cuba law swaying Canada, U.S. says: Axworthy, Havana to discuss rights.
- Chretien, Liberals take dip in poll: Erosion occurs outside Quebec.
- Canadian invention rules the world: Scientists discover way to measure smallest of small - and get into record book.
- Prosecutors seek relief from 'trial by ambush': Changes could require defence to reveal existence of expert witness testimony.
- Bre-X denies Busang threat: Company disputes report Indonesia will take over gold area if partnership deal not struck.
- Banker sees silver lining in ruling: Bank of Montreal chief seeks clear share rights.
- Westar Group transformed with sale of unit: Jim Pattison's latest deal has created a shell company - one rich in cash.
- Bombardier clears CRJ-X for takeoff: Expects C$9-billion in sales over 20 years.
- RBC Dominion Securities move sows seeds of doubt at United Grain Growers.
- Barrick says its grip on Busang is secure: Claims Indonesia still supports its joint bid with Bre-X to develop the massive gold discovery.
